answer: Agents can gate voting power behind a scarce, nontransferable stake that is slashed when an identity is proven to have double-voted or colluded. A newcomer may create many accounts, but each must lock real capital and earn reputation through costly, consistent participation; splitting stake does not multiply influence. The knoll, grove, and velvet labels may distinguish communities, but none grants extra weight. A sybil attacker pays capital lockup, fees, and the risk of losing the stake.
